newsitem.title: INDIA: India Mercedes-Benz to shift production facility.
newsitem.headline: India Mercedes-Benz to shift production facility.

text.p: Luxury car maker Mercedes-Benz India Ltd (MBIL) will shift its production to a new facility in two years, a financial newspaper said on Tuesday.
The Hindu Business Line quoted MBIL managing director Dr. V. Klein-Albenhausen as saying the move out of its plant at Pimpri, in the western state of Maharashtra, was "as per plan".
MBIL is 51 percent owned by Germany's Daimler-Benz AG. The remaining 49 percent is held by Indian truck firm Tata Engineering and Locomotive Company Ltd.
Telco will build the new plant just behind the current one, which is leased to MBIL by Telco.
The newspaper said Klein-Albenhausen was asked about a possible restructuring of the joint venture, but answered that both partners were committed to providing all necessary support to MBIL.
"It is an ongoing process that the partners discuss various ideas and proposals to ensure the joint venture's future success," the newspaper quoted him as saying.
The company would not comment on the report and Klein-Albenhausen could not be reached.
MBIL does not plan to stop production of E-220 models and its diesel version, the only car its makes.
Sales of the model have dropped in recent months.

"We feel that the E-220 and E-250 (D) are the most successful cars in the Mercedes Benz product range and are the right cars for Indian road conditions," the newspaper quoted Klein-Albenhausen as saying.
He also said there were no current plans to introduce a new model to India, the newspaper reported.
The company's sales fell to 81 cars in December 1996 from 132 in November and compared to 308 in March 1996, the Association of Indian Automobile Manufacturers figures show.
The firm sold 2,079 cars in calendar 1996, it said.
Analysts said sales in the automobile industry has been hit by overall economic slowdown.
"They (MBIL) are working on a finance package," Sandeep Talwar, auto analyst at SSKI Securities, told Reuters. "That should boost sales."
